utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T The Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for today starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours. Mark Harmon, Ann Sutherland, Carmela Javier for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Milos Androvic, Daniela Tasic, Mr. Gregor Guy-Smith and Novak Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry to come up with a housekeeping matter in the middle of a witness's testimony, but because of the urgency of the matter, I thought we might as well deal with it now. Could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Tesic. Sorry to have kept you waiting for another five minutes. We were doing a few things. Once again, I remind you that you are bound by the declaration you made at the beginning of your testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, before we finished yesterday afternoon, I asked you at transcript page 2051 what you and your unit were doing in Vogosca in January in 1994. You didn't have an opportunity to complete your answer before we broke for the day. I'd like to continue on that topic, but I first want to ask you a couple of preliminary questions. What was combat group BG-1?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not recollect now, unless I see a document referring to it, because it was a long time ago. In one of yesterday's documents, if I remember correctly, I think it's a part of the military police who were in Vogosca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Part of the military police of the VJ unit that went to Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What was your position when you arrived at Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was an operations officer, and I was appointed to that duty at the Guards Brigade of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And did your position change through the month of July?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which month?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I said July. January 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I continued to be an operations officer at the command of the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In that position, what were you doing? What tasks did you have?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I acted exclusively on the orders of the commander of the Guards Brigade when I went to tour units, when I monitored work of the brigade and reported to the commander. And when I was at the command, all I did was I kept the documentation, which according to regulations had to be kept at the command.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, may we move into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 24 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P353 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this is the war diary, at B/C/S, page 17, and the English, page 18. Mr. Tesic, this is an entry for the 20th of January, 1994, at the bottom of the page in the B/C/S. You wrote this entry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And that's your signature beside the entry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And here it states that you are the Chief of Staff of BG-1?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can you tell us which one to look at in the English, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. The first one: "Pursuant to" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yeah, and then halfway down that entry: "(NS of the BG-1 - Lieutenant-Colonel Tesic."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, are you able to explain this entry?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it reads, Chief of Staff. Maybe a comma is missing or something. I couldn't be Chief of Staff, nor could I be parallelly appointed Chief of Staff, if according to establishment, the Chief of Staff already exists in the Guards Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's Chief of Staff of combat group 1, BG-1?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. That's what's written here, but I'm telling you, I was not the Chief of Staff, and I stand by it. There was no order appointing me to that position, and I wouldn't say this is really intended this way, but I don't know how to explain it. I never noticed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But you wrote the entry, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. But I really don't know what to say. I can't explain it because I know I wasn't Chief of Staff. Maybe I made a mistake. Maybe I was thinking about something else when I was writing this. That happens. Normally, I'm rather precise in my work, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not want to speak before the witness's answer in order not to sound as leading, but I believe when a proper translation is done of the B/C/S, we'll see there are certain discrepancies. BG could be something referring to the case of a noun. You see, there is nothing between NS and BG-1. There is no word as -- such as "of."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, that may be so. Thank you very much for your assistance. But we've got the author of the story here. He can explain what he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, can you read, please, the entry starting with the word "officers," or starting with the sentence relating to the officers going to the -- to the forward end of the line just before it says NS of BG-1?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can't see the second word "order, presence of commanding officers on the forward" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness be asked to read slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Tesic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slowly. Go slowly. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Order. The next word is unclear, I can't make it out. It is my handwriting but I can't make it out. "Presence of commanding officers on the forward line until further notice." Then "NS," Nesa [phoen], that is, Chief of Staff of combat group 1, dash or something, "Lieutenant-Colonel Tesic; commander of the 2nd Motorised Battalion Major Borovcanin and other officers from the 2nd Motorised Battalion; engineering company and reconnaissance company)".

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, do you recall on the 20th of January, 1994, going to the forward line with Major Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. After all this time, I really couldn't remember, although it's written here, but I personally don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is a BG group?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I'm not sure if this is part of the police, that is, part of the police battalion that was present in Vogosca or some other unit. I wouldn't know until I look through the entire diary to see if it repeats often. But there are frequent references to BG-1, and in fact, we put it in as the commander instructed us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What are the functions of a BG group, a combat group?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know who was in charge of BG-1?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which combat group it was, so I couldn't tell you what it consisted of or who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sir, it was combat group 1. Let's tell you. We are talking about combat group 1. You had 2 and others, but so if you say you don't know which one you're talking, it is -- we can only describe it by saying it's combat group 1. Are you able to answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. You saw a document on Monday, Exhibit P355, which was a document dated the 5th of January from Stojimirovic, which states that the 72nd Special Brigade handed over the area of responsibility to the Guards Brigade. Would this then mean that Stojimirovic would take over the responsibilities of Stupar who was the commander of the 72nd Special Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only give you my opinion here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think this is outside the scope of my cross-examination, and I think the witness is being asked to speculate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm trying to establish who the commander of BG-1 is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but don't invite speculation. The witness has just told you: "I can only give you my opinion here."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know -- okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could have Exhibit P359 on the screen, please. I'm sorry, terribly sorry. P355. And page number -- Your Honour, I'm told that the Exhibit that I want is Exhibit P359, but what came up -- yeah, I'm sorry. It was Exhibit P359. It was the document that you had on the screen initially. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If the exhibit you want is P359, do we still need to stay in private session? It's not under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, this document states that during the attack on the 27th of December, 1993, by the BG-1, i.e., the combat group 1, under the command of Colonel Stupar who was the commander of the 72nd Special Brigade, if, as we've just discussed, the Guards Brigade took over the responsibilities of the 72nd Brigade, do you know if they took over -- do you know whether Stojimirovic took over at commander of BG-1?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question. As for taking over the zone of the 72nd Brigade or, rather, that a handover took place between the 72nd Brigade and the Guards Brigade, that did happen; but I don't know if they remained to be referred to -- continued to be referred to as BG-1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You mentioned yesterday that --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I am sorry, Your Honour. We're going to have to go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. 6 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, can we conclude from the document that we just saw on the screen that a BG group is involved in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see it from this. I only said that the Guards Brigade took over part of the responsibilities from the 72nd Brigade and became part of the Defence forces of the Vogosca area and more broadly the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yesterday at transcript pages 2016 to 2017, you said that you agreed with Mr. Lukic that actions were planned but nothing was being carried out on the ground. You also said at page -- transcript page 2031 that the Guards Brigade didn't participate in offensive actions during their stay from the 31st of December, 1993, through to the 30th of January, 1994. But earlier in your testimony at transcript page 2014, you agreed with Mr. Lukic that there were combat activities, and I will read you the passage. The question was: "On the basis of what I've just showed you" - that was on transcript page 2013 - "do you agree with my thesis that in terms of your combat activities, your superior officers received their orders from the VRS command structure, in other words, from the commander of the SRK?" And you answered: "On the basis of this, such a statement could be deducted." So was the Guards Brigade involved in combat activities in January 1994?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the tasks that I mentioned was to destroy emerging targets ahead of the forward line and to respond to fire with fire. So there was sporadic fire, but the only point where the Guards Brigade arrived -- or, rather, part of the Guards Brigade or, more precisely, a couple of armoured combat vehicles was involved was to recapture part of Orlovo where members of the VRS had been killed in early morning hours, but there was no -- there was not much fighting because the ABiH forces had already withdrawn. It had been a sabotage attack at dawn. We can't say there wasn't any shooting, but I'm saying we can't really talk about proper operations because the Guards Brigade in those couple of months [as interpreted] did not participate in any offensive action, nor did it move from the positions that it took up on the 1st of January, 1994, that is, in the period from the 1st to the 5th of January, 1994, when the handover of that zone took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: You said a couple of months -- you said when the unit was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely what I wanted to correct. The witness actually said "in that month."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could have Exhibit P353 on the screen again, please. If we could go to page 7 of the English translation, which is an entry for the 5th of January, 1994. I think page 11 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one of the two? Is it 13 --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Entry number 13. Entry number 13, which will be on the preceding page, down at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, it says here: "The engagement of the units during the day was according to the plan." This is on the 5th of January. What was the plan?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment, I could not really recall what the plan was. It was the commander's plan, and this is just a note that everything was proceeding according to plan, and this has been confirmed by signature, but I cannot really recall after 15 years what really happened. Most probably, it concerns the takeover of the area of responsibility from the 72nd Special Brigade, and this is what is mentioned in the next sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to entry number 17, which is on page 9 of the English translation, and page 13, I think, of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, it says there under paragraph 2: "This unit shall carry out combat tasks as per the orders by the BG-1 commander."

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you explain what combat tasks were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, given the amount of time that elapsed, but I do believe that whatever happened during the day was recorded here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to entry number 19, which is on page 10 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It says there: "Previously set tasks still stand." And: "The BVP shall continue carrying out the present task." What is the BVP?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And just further down: "Other units to resume work on previously given tasks." Are you aware of what those previous tasks were?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume again, I cannot state for certain, but I presume that this goes for defence. Since nothing special was happening, we just note that previously set tasks continued - this is an entry done by my colleague Paunovic - and work should continue on preventing any slippage in the combat morale of our units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to entry number 20, the next entry. That's of the 11th of January, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "Offensive operations shall be continued along all directions." Do you remember what these offensive operations related to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says; offensive operations to be continued along all axes. I wouldn't know, but I do state that in the area where the Guards Brigade was located, and that is the area of Vogosca, there were no offensive actions, and we did not move.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It says, The main direction of the attack was Rajlovac and then two illegible words in the English translation, and then Brdo, which means "hill" in English. Do you know what was going on in that area on the 11th of January?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says the main axis of attack will be Rajlovac, Sokolje, Svabino Brdo, or Svabino Hill. While I was in Vogosca, I never went to Rajlovac, not once, and I don't know whether any of our units were there, and if there was an APC or armoured personnel carrier went there, it must have been issued -- an order issued by the commander, local commander there. What we did here was just note what was happening.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we can go to entry number 21, which is the -- dated the 13th of January, 1994. And, Your Honour, there is a mistake in the English translation. I went to entry 20, and I said it was dated the 11th of January. It's in fact the 12th of January. I can see that from the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, it says on the 13th of January at entry number 21: "The unit worked as in the plan." Again, are you able to recollect what the plan was that they were working to?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But nothing was happening, and this is reflected in the first sentence, which says: "No problems were encountered during the day."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Entry number 22, which is for the 14th of January, and again, we have a date of 11th of January in the English translation, which will be changed when it will be revised, so... At 2000 hours, the units worked in accordance with previously received tasks, and then further down: "Other units are engaged in active Defence with the task to inflict losses on the enemy." These entries would seem to -- would these entries seem to you to be putting into operation what was planned?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't want to object before the question is finished. It seems that the -- suggestions are being put to the witness. I do believe that this is within the scope of my cross-examination, but there is a series of questions whereby the Prosecution goes back into examination-in-chief mode. The witness said that he didn't remember some things. The Prosecution should address the questions that we put to the witness and not to explore certain matters which are contained in the war diary and which had been shown to him during examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: One moment, Your Honour. Your Honour, I'm addressing the question that was put by Mr. Lukic in relation to the witness. Mr. Lukic's question was: "It's very often they make mention of planning of combat operations, but I never see any entry explaining that a combat action has been executed." And the witness said: "Yes, actions were planned, but nothing was being carried out." I'm simply taking him to entries which may show that in fact the unit was working to a plan, so they were in fact putting some plan into operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for His Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shall I start again? So the problem is that your witness is consistently taking the position that nothing happened, and the re-examination appears to be like either cross-examination or an attempt to impeach. I'm not quite sure what is happening. What's happening? You are taking him now to entries, which I didn't think had been canvassed in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Some of the entries were but not those particular sentences, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Some of the entries were what?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Some of the entries have been covered in examination-in-chief but not those particular sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's my point. That's the point. But, you know, I think you've taken the witness through quite a number of entries and he's sticking by his position. Just be careful not to be cross-examining or to be re-leading, trying to put in new evidence. I am sympathetic to the objection, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. May we go to entry number -- the entry for the 17th of January, which -- if we could go to page 14 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's the entry number, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It doesn't -- in the box where it is, it doesn't have an entry number, but it's two boxes below what I think is entry number 26. It's got a back slash, question mark, back slash, 6, and then two boxes down from that, so that's on page 13, and the following page is page 14 where it has "Vogosca, 17th of January, 1994, at 2000 hours."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, under the words "orders for 18 January 1994," you referred earlier this morning about one operation, if I can put it. Was this the operation that you were talking about in relation to combat where there's reference to launching an attack along the axis in cooperation with BG-2 and facilitating the attack of BG-2, and then further down: "The forces of the 2nd Motorised Battalion are to provide fire support..." Is that the incident that you were talking about earlier this morning?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to entry number 31. This is the last entry that I will take you to. It's on page 17 of the English translation. It's the 18th of January, 1994, at 2000 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In this entry we can see: "During the day, the units were carrying out their respective assignments. Our units were actively engaged in sniper and mortar fire along the line." Was this the incident that you were referring to this morning?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't refer to that area. This is a completely different area above the town of Orlovo where, I repeat, there was a sabotage attack to the lines held by the VRS. After losses incurred, the commander of the Guards Brigade decided upon invitation to send a part of the military police unit to stabilize the line and to return men to the previously held positions; and by appearing there, given the snowy conditions and the appearance of those APCs, our combat armoured vehicles, really nothing happened. What happened here as described is the firing of mortar shells in front of our frontline or forward positions. These high elevations, 772 and elevation 830, this is ahead -- the area in front of the Vogosca Brigade positions where parts of our 2nd Battalion were, and it is true that fire was open, but there was no attack launched. There were no attack activities going on. Most probably, we responded to fire by fire. Most probably, but I cannot state it as a fact after 15 years. It will be with pleasure that I would assist you if I could, but I took a solemn declaration that I will speak the truth and not lies.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, how do you know that there were no attack activities going on on this particular day?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what you showed me. I'm discussing that. It is stated here that there were sniper and mortar fire. Most probably, they were responding to fire by fire, but the opening of fire does not concern the area of Srednje which was held by - I don't know - a brigade of the VRS, and this is the area which is above the town called Orlovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. I'll move on to another topic. We discussed in the war diary certain entries in relation to the training of snipers for the Ilidza and the Rajlovac brigades. I won't take you to them, but they were the dates of the 11th and the 15th and the 17th of January. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Are you aware of -- well, can you just explain for the Trial Chamber what a sniper rifle is?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sniper rifle, just as any other piece of weaponry, is a personal arms of an individual soldier. Its calibre is 7.9 millimetres with an optical sight, and an individual soldier will be responsible for such a rifle. In the VJ, any conscript will be given a weapon, a rifle, when he enters the national service and be responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: What is the maximum effective range of a sniper rifle?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maximum range is up to 5 kilometres. With an optical sight, you can hit targets up to 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Where is --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Actually, if we could have Rule 65 ter 09244, which is a map, on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While this map is coming, can I just ask for my own lessons. I know very little about war and arms and ammunition. When you say maximum range is up to 5 kilometres, and that with an optical sight you can hit the target at 1.000 metres, does it mean if it goes beyond 1.000 metres but within the range of 5 kilometres you can't hit the target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the round or the bullet has a parabolic curve, and this is the maximum range of that bullet if -- when fired. But this is not the way that a marksman will use to destroy his target when he's searching for targets. The other range, 1.000 metres on your optical sights, you have distances from you to the target; and on the basis of that, you can hit the target. You can try to hit it. The marksman will assess the distance, sets the elements on the optical sight, and will pull the trigger at the most appropriate moment. Best results can be achieved between 600 and 700 metres, and I'm talking about the sniper rifles available to the VJ at the time. Other weapons, automatic rifles are most effective until up to 400 metres, single rounds, if single rounds are fired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks for the lesson.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, can you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we enlarge the map a little more. Not quite that much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we still need to be in closed session, ma'am? Madam Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, where is Ilidza located --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, counsel. Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, where is Ilidza located on this map, and if you could put a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where the frontline for that brigade was?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know its area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a completely different area. This is the -- on the opposite side of Sarajevo from where we were, from where our positions were.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where -- where is Rajlovac located?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could you circle that, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know where the frontline for that brigade was?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never went there, and I recently told you that I never went to Rajlovac while I was there at Vogosca, neither do I know the position of that unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. Could you put a number 1 next to Ilidza and a number 2 next to Rajlovac, please.

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender that map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P370, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I've finished with the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, yesterday at transcript page 2018, you said that you wore your VJ uniform while you were in Vogosca. Were non-commissioned officers and soldiers, to your knowledge, ordered not to wear VJ uniform?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have such information. There we all wore VJ uniforms. I never saw anybody in civilian clothes, I mean, those members who were at Vogosca at this time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Do you know if they were ordered to remove their insignia of the VJ?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of such an order.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: On the uniforms of the officers, NCOs, and soldiers, did you see the VJ insignia?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't claim I've seen that. I don't remember even if I wore insignia or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: How long did you think that you would be staying in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally, and I'm speaking only in my own name, expected to stay 15 to 20 days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: For such a short mission, would there normally be 200 men, three tanks and other equipment sent?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the second part of the Guards Brigade that appeared in Vogosca on the 31st. I cannot talk about the first part of the Guards Brigade that left in mid-December 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: For such a short mission, would 120 men and three tanks and other -- a lot of other heavy equipment be sent on such a mission?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tanks came from the armament brigade, not the Guards Brigade, and I found them there. They were already there when I arrived. As for the rest of the weaponry, it was the weaponry and equipment normally in possession of the units of the Army of Yugoslavia. Nothing was carried there that was not prescribed by establishment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to the Pancir-2 operation --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we have exhibit -- I'm sorry, Rule 65 ter number 08382 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My first objection is that this document, although it is on the 65 ter list, has not been notified to us as one of the documents to be used with this witness. I don't know if it has been shown to the witness at all. I see no connection with the cross-examination, but for the time being, my objection is that we were not notified this document would be used with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are in re-examination at the moment. We are not obliged to advise the Defence of documents we are going to put in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What's your authority for that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My problem is that it looks like you're leading evidence anew, for me. You're coming up with exhibits that you didn't canvass in chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is as a result of cross-examination, Your Honour. If we can go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sutherland, I'm still dealing with an objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: But in order to -- Mr. Lukic in closed session took the witness to a passage, and I want to follow up on that passage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm still dealing with an objection, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So you are not going to order me to go into private session when I'm still dealing with an objection that comes from the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. I was saying to you, you appear to me to be leading evidence anew. Do you have any comment to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this evidence is in relation to what was raised in cross-examination, and I think it's legitimate to go over it in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but you go over it on re-examination on the issues that you dealt with it in chief, not new evidence. You don't call new evidence into examination, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, re-examination deals with matters raised in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This was a matter raised in cross-examination which I want to deal with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what is this matter that you want to deal with that was raised in cross-examination? What is the issue?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Pancir-2 operation. Mr. Lukic took the witness to certain matters in closed session, and I wish to take the witness to that and ask him another question in relation to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But what is the relevance of 65 ter 08382 in that matter, which was not shown to the witness before?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's relevant to exactly the question put to the witness by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like you to canvass that before you call this document up.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could we go into closed session so that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into closed session. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, I have to object to the method applied yesterday. I would prefer that the witness be asked the question and then shown a document rather than the other way around. Perhaps my objection was premature, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's just what I have just said. Before this exhibit is put on the screen, canvass the point, Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 13 [Closed session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Trial Chamber I]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, may I just for the record that we are in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. I was trying to do it without going back into closed session to put the question that was put to Mr. Lukic, but I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do listen when you are communicating either with anybody in response to what is being said.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, at transcript page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can this document please be removed from the screen. Could we please remove it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, at transcript page 2029 to 2030, Mr. Lukic put his position in relation to the Pancir operation and read out to you a number of brigades that were involved in Pancir-2 operation and said that -- mentioned the Vogosca Brigade, the Rajlovac Brigade, one brigade from the Krajina Corps, one brigade of the Herzegovina corps, 500 members of the police of the Republika Srpska who took part in it. That was Mr. Lukic's -- part of Mr. Lukic's question, and then asked: "Do you agree with me that those units represented a substantial force of an army in an operation in such an area?" And then you replied: "Yes." "And you would also note that we had the Kosevo Brigade as well?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then Mr. Lukic asked you -- or told you: "And from the VJ, the Army of Yugoslavia, who was present there in accordance with my thesis and my information in the first group that was led by Colonel Stupar, there were 120 men, and then there was the other group which came with your unit, so to bring the total slightly above 200 men who were engaged in that action; isn't that correct?" And you answered yes. You said: "That's correct." My question to you is, was there also a helicopter squad involved in the Pancir-2 operation?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: When you were in Vogosca, did you see a helicopter squad at the logistics base?

utterances.speaker: BORIVOJE TESIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Tesic, that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Let me take this time to thank you for taking the time off your schedule - I'm sure you must be a busy person even though you are retired - to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down. May you please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much for these kind words. I wish you success in your work, and I am happy if I was of any assistance to the Prosecution and the Defence in coming to the truth. Thank you again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May we please move into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you get assistance with the window, please. Thank you. Yes, Madam Sutherland. Is this a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I would like to advise the Court that we do not -- the next witness is not available until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does this then bring us to the end of the day?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Then we stand adjourned to tomorrow at 9.00 in the morning, same courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 27th of November, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.14 a.m.,
